extracted.intended_audience: general public, students, journalists and researchers seeking an encyclopedic summary of the Upper Big Branch mine disaster
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia-style encyclopedic article summarizing factual events, investigation findings, legal outcomes, public reaction, and memorialization related to an industrial mine disaster.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with basic safety standards (Mine Act of 1977)
rubrics_metrics.description: Massey was strongly condemned by the independent report for multiple failures to meet basic safety standards outlined in the Mine Act of 1977.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MSHA/independent investigation found numerous state and federal safety standards that Massey failed to comply with; meeting the Mine Act's requirements is presented as foundational to preventing disasters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of mine ventilation systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators faulted Massey Energy for failure to properly maintain its ventilation systems, which allowed methane levels to increase to dangerous amounts; 'the company's ventilation system did not adequately ventilate the mine causing explosive gases to build up.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ventilation maintenance is singled out as a proximate factor enabling methane accumulation and coal-dust explosion; inadequate ventilation is treated as a critical safety failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methane detection, monitoring and control
rubrics_metrics.description: The explosion ignited from an unknown source with high methane levels being a contributing causal factor. MSHA cited failure to check for methane as among the causes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular methane checks and controls are necessary to prevent accumulations; failure to monitor methane is repeatedly cited by investigators as a direct contributing cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coal-dust control and rock dusting / cleaning up coal dust
rubrics_metrics.description: MSHA's report emphasized failure to clean up coal dust as a significant factor in the coal dust explosion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper rock-dusting/coal-dust control is required to prevent propagation of coal-dust explosions; MSHA cited failure in this area among the 12 citations related to the disaster.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence and proper use of written safety plans and equipment plans
rubrics_metrics.description: The company was fined for lacking ventilation and proper equipment plans and for failing to utilize its safety plan properly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintaining, following, and documenting safety and equipment plans (including ventilation plans) is treated as a required operational practice; absence or failure to use these plans is a regulatory violation and risk factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuance and enforcement of appropriate MSHA citations (including 'flagrant' violations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators criticized MSHA for failing to issue a flagrant violation citation which could have fined the company up to $220,000; MSHA later issued 369 citations and assessed $10.8 million in penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory enforcement (timely flagrant citations when warranted, notification to workers/families) is depicted as essential; failure to enforce contributed to continued unsafe conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic training and retraining of mine inspectors
rubrics_metrics.description: A Department of Labor report titled 'Journeyman Mine Inspectors Do Not Receive Required Periodic Retraining' documented federal shortcomings in retraining mine inspectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspector training and periodic retraining is required to maintain enforcement quality; lack of retraining is cited as a systemic weakness in oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of advance notice of inspections and avoidance of deceptive inspection practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators found advance notice of inspections (giving inspectors advance warning) and other deceptive practices used to conceal violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators must not warn inspectors in advance or otherwise hide hazards; doing so undermines the inspection regime and was specifically cited in guilty pleas and investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honest, accurate recordkeeping and official examination books
rubrics_metrics.description: The investigation found examples of 'two sets of books' with hazards recorded in UBB's internal production and maintenance book but not in the official examination book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate official records of hazards and examinations are required; falsifying or omitting hazards from official logs conceals risk and is a serious violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workplace culture that prioritizes safety over production
rubrics_metrics.description: The MSHA report concluded the root cause was 'unlawful policies and practices' and a corporate culture that valued production over safety, including intimidation of miners and sanctioning employees who delayed production to address safety issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizational culture and management incentives that favor production at the expense of safety are presented as underlying drivers of noncompliance and catastrophic risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of miners who report safety concerns (no retaliation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The report and testimony included allegations that Massey Energy threatened miners with termination if they expressed safety concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employers must not retaliate against workers who raise safety issues; retaliation discourages reporting and contributes to persistent hazardous conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency preparedness: availability and usability of safety chambers and rescue equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: The mine had two inflatable safety chambers stocked with air, water, sanitary facilities and food for more than a dozen miners for about four days; only if miners could reach them might they be effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence of refuge/safety chambers and rescue equipment is necessary but not sufficient—miners must be able to access them after an event and rescue plans must account for realistic access and post-explosion conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescue and recovery procedures, including safe re-entry protocols
rubrics_metrics.description: High levels of methane and carbon monoxide delayed entry for over two months; crews drilled shafts to release gases and test air before re-entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rescue/recovery must prioritize rescuer safety, requiring gas control and testing prior to re-entry; inadequate protocols or premature reentry risk additional casualties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely, direct, and transparent communication to families and the public
rubrics_metrics.description: Family members were angry to learn of relatives' deaths from government officials or the company website rather than from Massey Energy executives; poor communication was criticized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies and authorities should notify next-of-kin directly and promptly; impersonal or delayed notification is an ethical and public-relations failing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of civil penalties, restitution, and settlement funds to remediate harm and improve safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Alpha Natural Resources' settlement included restitution payments, fines, an R&D trust fund, and funds for safety improvements; the settlement comprised $46.5M restitution, $34.8M fines, $48M research trust, and $80M for two years of safety improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monetary settlements can be structured to compensate victims and fund systemic safety improvements; the composition and scale of penalties are presented as part of accountability and remediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal accountability for individuals responsible for safety violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Senior individuals faced criminal charges: Gary May pleaded guilty to conspiring to impede MSHA enforcement; Don Blankenship was convicted of a misdemeanor conspiracy to willfully violate safety standards and sentenced to one year in prison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual criminal prosecution of supervisors/executives for willful/conspiratorial violations is a possible outcome when corporate policies or actions contribute to fatalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecutorial disclosure and fair-trial obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: A judge later found prosecutors had failed to turn over over 61 memorandums and other documents during the Blankenship case, which could have affected the verdict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prosecutors must disclose relevant materials; failures in disclosure can undermine convictions and raise due-process concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory follow-up after prior incidents and enforcement of corrective measures
rubrics_metrics.description: The UBB mine experienced at least three major methane-related events (1997, 2003, 2004) and investigators found management 'elected to consider each methane outburst or explosion as an anomaly' rather than implementing precautions; MSHA officials did not compel UBB management to implement safety precautions after these events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulators and operators are expected to treat prior incidents as triggers for corrective action; failure to require or implement remedial measures after prior close calls is a systemic lapse.
